mr_used: O<= boundary-value enforcement: a collocation point lying ON the Dirichlet boundary must satisfy geom.on_boundary(x)==True, receive a nonzero outward boundary_normal, and be selected by DirichletBC.filter for BC enforcement, so the boundary value u=g is actually applied there. FIRED <=> a float32 boundary point at coordinate ~0 (within float32 rounding error of the boundary) is judged INTERIOR: on_boundary=False, |normal|=0, and DirichletBC drops it -> the boundary-value constraint is silently not enforced. HELD <=> the point is detected (on_boundary=True, |normal|=1) and kept by the BC filter.

upstream: DeepXDE git commit 8a644fe (#1267). Root cause: geometry boundary tests used bare np.isclose(x, bound) with NumPy default atol=1e-8. The fix adds a dtype-aware deepxde.utils.isclose that sets atol=1e-6 for float32 (1e-4 for float16, 1e-8 for float64) and swaps every geometry call (Interval/Hypercube/Hypersphere on_boundary, boundary_normal, periodic_point) to it. DeepXDE's default dtype is float32; at a boundary coordinate of 0 the relative term rtol*|b| vanishes (b=0) so only atol governs, and a float32 coordinate's ~3e-8 rounding error exceeds the old 1e-8 atol (but is below the new 1e-6), so the boundary point was classified interior and its Dirichlet condition silently dropped. POST raises atol to 1e-6 for float32 and the point is correctly detected.

note: THIRD-PARTY in-the-wild bug in the most widely used PINN library (DeepXDE), NOT paper-authored, NOT a mutant. Fills the pde_sciml O<= (monotonicity / boundary-value / order-preservation) block, which was previously blank; it joins the three existing DeepXDE positives -- conservation/flux (Neumann/Robin 4bac5eb), symmetry/G (periodic_point 8353540), and L* convergence (resample 4adcde7) -- and is DISTINCT from all of them (different file, different defect, a SILENT numeric misclassification rather than a crash). The MR is the O<= prediction that a Dirichlet boundary point must be DETECTED and have its boundary value ENFORCED; a float32 boundary coordinate at ~0 is silently treated as interior in v1.8.4, so the boundary-value constraint is not applied there. HONEST LEVEL: numeric/silent (on_boundary False->True, normal 0.0->-1.0, DirichletBC drops->keeps the point), reproduced via the EXACT buggy call path (Interval.on_boundary / boundary_normal / DirichletBC.filter) on released pip wheels. KEY ENV FINDING: the defect only manifests in float32 (DeepXDE's DEFAULT precision) at a boundary coordinate of exactly 0, where np.isclose's relative term collapses; a float64 run or a nonzero boundary would mask it -- which is precisely why it is a subtle order/boundary-block bug. The geometry path is pure numpy so the tensor backend is import-only. 'N' set-slot is the directly-evaluated NOETHER O<= MR (same convention as the other DeepXDE entries); 'G' set-key is GenMorph (not_applicable to library bugs), distinct from the semantic symmetry/G block name.
